title: Which Past? - Scene or Event
description: Choose between {j'étais} and {j'ai mangé} when you talk about the past.
can_do: Say how things were in the past with {j'étais} and {j'avais}.
line: The imparfait sets the scene, and the passé composé tells what happened.

parts.heading: Scene and event
text: French has two tenses for telling a story in the past. The imparfait ({j'étais}, {j'avais}) sets the scene: how things were. The passé composé ({j'ai mangé}) tells what happened.

parts.heading: The scene, then the event
text: A past story often starts with the scene and then moves to what happened.

build.fr: J'avais faim et j'ai mangé une pomme.
build.en: I was hungry and I ate an apple.

lines: Hier soir, nous étions au café. Nous avons mangé un croissant.
Last night we were at the café. We ate a croissant.
Marie avait faim et elle a mangé une banane.
Marie was hungry and she ate a banana.
J'ai mangé une pizza. C'était très bon.
I ate a pizza. It was very good.

parts.heading: One question to ask
text: Ask yourself: is this how things were, or something that happened?
parts.note: The imparfait answers the first: {j'étais}, {il avait}. The passé composé answers the second: {j'ai mangé}.

checks.ask: Listen. Does this set the scene or tell what happened?
checks.why: {J'avais faim} says how things were, so it takes the imparfait.

checks.ask: Which one means “I ate an apple”?
checks.why: Eating the apple is something that happened, so it takes the passé composé: {j'ai mangé}.

checks.ask: Which one means “Yesterday, Paul was hungry”?
checks.why: Being hungry is how things were, so it takes the imparfait: {Paul avait faim}.
